{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Implement U1 by extending the existing Spring XD landing page and navigation structure rather than introducing a new frontend framework.",
    "Implement retry classification in RabbitMessageBus using configurable exception types, matching configured exceptions by assignability so subclasses are also handled.",
    "Support retry configuration at both bus and stream deployment levels, with stream-level settings taking precedence over bus-level defaults.",
    "Treat Kryo deserialization failures as non-retryable by default, while retaining configuration support for overriding or extending the non-retryable exception set.",
    "Preserve existing public configuration names and behavior wherever possible, and provide backward-compatible defaults for upgraded Spring Integration, Kafka, and Hadoop dependencies.",
    "Expose module and container identifiers through the existing module execution context or environment abstraction, and make the identifiers available to logging through a standard accessor and logging context integration.",
    "Implement Kafka consumer and producer override properties as module-level settings layered over Kafka bus defaults, with explicit precedence and validation for unsupported values.",
    "Update dependency versions through the existing build and dependency-management mechanism rather than copying libraries into individual modules.",
    "Keep XD and XD plus Ambari RPM build scripts in a single public repository with separate, clearly documented build entry points and shared script components where practical.",
    "Use automated unit, integration, build, and regression tests for the affected transport, module, UI, dependency, and packaging behavior."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The existing Spring XD source repository, build system, web UI, RabbitMQ transport, Kafka transport, module deployment model, and RPM scripts are available and buildable before changes begin.",
    "The increment is implemented against the existing Spring XD codebase and its established Java and Maven conventions; no migration to a different framework or build system is required.",
    "U1 requires a simple landing-page navigation enhancement only; no new authentication, authorization, responsive redesign, or information architecture overhaul is required.",
    "The requested Spring Integration, SI Kafka, and Spring Hadoop versions are compatible with the target Spring XD baseline, or only localized compatibility fixes are needed.",
    "Dependency upgrades include source and binary compatibility remediation, test updates, and build verification, but do not include upgrading unrelated third-party libraries.",
    "For U2, configured exception names are loadable from the runtime classpath and invalid class names produce a clear configuration error.",
    "For U2, a retryable exception configuration is evaluated when a message delivery fails, before the existing retry and recovery behavior is invoked.",
    "For U6, module and container identifiers already exist in deployment metadata or runtime context and only need to be exposed consistently to module code and logging.",
    "For U7, the listed Kafka properties map to the existing consumer and producer configuration model; no new Kafka client protocol features are required.",
    "For U8, the public repository can be created or modified by the developer, and repository administration, legal review, and long-term release management are outside the implementation effort.",
    "Documentation is limited to configuration reference, upgrade notes, examples, and build instructions for the changed functionality.",
    "Effort includes implementation, code review preparation, automated tests, integration verification, and developer documentation, but excludes elapsed waiting time and work by other teams."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Repository analysis and increment design",
      "activity_description": "Inspect the existing XD web application, module deployment context, RabbitMQ and Kafka transports, dependency management, test conventions, and RPM build layout. Produce the detailed implementation plan, configuration precedence rules, compatibility approach, and test strategy for all eight user stories.",
      "most_likely_effort": 20
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Landing page navigation for sources, processors, sinks, and jobs",
      "activity_description": "Add higher-order links to the existing landing page, connect them to the correct source, processor, sink, and job sections, preserve current routing and styling conventions, and add focused UI or controller tests as supported by the existing project.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Configurable RabbitMessageBus retry exception handling",
      "activity_description": "Implement bus-level and stream-deployment-level retryable or non-retryable exception configuration, define precedence and validation, integrate classification with RabbitMQ delivery retry handling, support messaging and AMQP conversion exception scenarios, disable retries for Kryo deserialization failures by default, and add unit and transport-level tests covering inheritance, configuration errors, and retry exhaustion behavior.",
      "most_likely_effort": 72
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Spring Integration 4.1.5 upgrade",
      "activity_description": "Update dependency management to Spring Integration 4.1.5, resolve compilation and behavioral compatibility issues, verify message-channel behavior and affected module integrations, update tests where APIs or semantics changed, and document the upgrade.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "SI Kafka extension 1.2.0 upgrade",
      "activity_description": "Upgrade the Spring Integration Kafka extension to 1.2.0, adapt Kafka module configuration or APIs as required, verify producer and consumer startup and message flow, and add or update compatibility and regression tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Spring Hadoop 2.2.0 GA upgrade",
      "activity_description": "Update Spring Hadoop dependencies to the 2.2.0 GA release, remediate API or configuration incompatibilities in Hadoop-related modules, execute representative Hadoop integration tests or available test doubles, and update upgrade documentation.",
      "most_likely_effort": 48
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Module and container identifier access",
      "activity_description": "Expose the unique module ID and container ID to newly developed source, processor, and sink components through the established runtime context or environment API. Integrate the values with logging context where appropriate, define behavior when an identifier is unavailable, and add unit and deployment-level tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 48
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Kafka consumer and producer bus-default overrides",
      "activity_description": "Add module consumer overrides for autoCommitEnabled, queueSize, maxWait, and fetchSize, and producer overrides for batchSize and batchTimeout. Implement configuration binding, validation, precedence over bus defaults, propagation to Kafka client or SI Kafka configuration, backward-compatible defaults, and comprehensive unit and integration tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 64
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Unified public repository and RPM build scripts",
      "activity_description": "Consolidate the XD and XD plus Ambari RPM scripts into one public repository structure, preserve independent build workflows, remove or adapt duplicated path assumptions, add repository-level build documentation, and verify clean builds for both script sets.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Cross-feature regression and integration verification",
      "activity_description": "Run the complete build and relevant integration suites, including RabbitMQ retry scenarios, Kafka property overrides, module and container identifier propagation, upgraded Spring Integration/Kafka/Hadoop modules, landing-page navigation, and RPM packaging. Diagnose and fix regressions found during verification.",
      "most_likely_effort": 72
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "Documentation, release notes, and final implementation cleanup",
      "activity_description": "Finalize configuration reference material, deployment examples, retry and Kafka precedence documentation, identifier usage guidance for module developers, dependency upgrade notes, RPM repository instructions, release notes, and final code cleanup for delivery.",
      "most_likely_effort": 20
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 488
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Implement U1 by extending the existing Spring XD landing page and navigation structure rather than introducing a new frontend framework.
Implement retry classification in RabbitMessageBus using configurable exception types, matching configured exceptions by assignability so subclasses are also handled.
Support retry configuration at both bus and stream deployment levels, with stream-level settings taking precedence over bus-level defaults.
Treat Kryo deserialization failures as non-retryable by default, while retaining configuration support for overriding or extending the non-retryable exception set.
Preserve existing public configuration names and behavior wherever possible, and provide backward-compatible defaults for upgraded Spring Integration, Kafka, and Hadoop dependencies.

Expose module and container identifiers through the existing module execution context or environment abstraction, and make the identifiers available to logging through a standard accessor and logging context integration.
Implement Kafka consumer and producer override properties as module-level settings layered over Kafka bus defaults, with explicit precedence and validation for unsupported values.
Update dependency versions through the existing build and dependency-management mechanism rather than copying libraries into individual modules.
Keep XD and XD plus Ambari RPM build scripts in a single public repository with separate, clearly documented build entry points and shared script components where practical.
Use automated unit, integration, build, and regression tests for the affected transport, module, UI, dependency, and packaging behavior.
assumptions: The existing Spring XD source repository, build system, web UI, RabbitMQ transport, Kafka transport, module deployment model, and RPM scripts are available and buildable before changes begin.
The increment is implemented against the existing Spring XD codebase and its established Java and Maven conventions; no migration to a different framework or build system is required.
U1 requires a simple landing-page navigation enhancement only; no new authentication, authorization, responsive redesign, or information architecture overhaul is required.
The requested Spring Integration, SI Kafka, and Spring Hadoop versions are compatible with the target Spring XD baseline, or only localized compatibility fixes are needed.
Dependency upgrades include source and binary compatibility remediation, test updates, and build verification, but do not include upgrading unrelated third-party libraries.
For U2, configured exception names are loadable from the runtime classpath and invalid class names produce a clear configuration error.
For U2, a retryable exception configuration is evaluated when a message delivery fails, before the existing retry and recovery behavior is invoked.
For U6, module and container identifiers already exist in deployment metadata or runtime context and only need to be exposed consistently to module code and logging.
For U7, the listed Kafka properties map to the existing consumer and producer configuration model; no new Kafka client protocol features are required.
For U8, the public repository can be created or modified by the developer, and repository administration, legal review, and long-term release management are outside the implementation effort.
Documentation is limited to configuration reference, upgrade notes, examples, and build instructions for the changed functionality.
Effort includes implementation, code review preparation, automated tests, integration verification, and developer documentation, but excludes elapsed waiting time and work by other teams.
